title: From Samples to Scenarios: A New Paradigm for Probabilistic Forecasting
claim: Sampling-based approaches have clear limitations; a new paradigm of explicit scenario-probability pairs addresses them and is validated by a simple model.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, arrows linking motivation, solution, evaluation, rounded-border boxes
description: A wide banner figure with a gradient-colored title, 'Forecasting Beyond Sampling: A New Paradigm'. Three rounded panels run left to right and are linked by gradient arrows. The orange Motivation panel has a warning icon and the heading 'Limitations of Sampling'. It lists three icon-labeled problems: (i) Probability Absence, (ii) Coverage Inadequacy and (iii) Inference Cost. The blue Solution panel is titled 'Probabilistic Scenarios'. It shows (i) {Scenario, Probability} with percentage-labeled mini plots, (ii) Diverse Scenarios with a forecast fan plot, and (iii) Single Forward Pass with {y1,p1}...{yN,pN} pairs. The green Evaluation panel is labeled 'Proof-of-Concept'. It shows a scales icon, the TimePrism logo and three checkmarked claims: a simple linear model, built with Probabilistic Scenarios, and competitive against SOTAs. The color shift from orange to blue to green carries the eye through the argument.
caption: Motivation, solution, and evaluation of this work. We illustrate the limitations of the prevailing sampling-based paradigm for probabilistic forecasting. In response, we introduce Probabilistic Scenarios, a new paradigm that directly produces a set of {Scenario, Probability} pairs, and validate its potential with a simple proof-of-concept model, TimePrism.
abstract: Most state-of-the-art probabilistic time series forecasting models rely on sampling to represent future uncertainty. However, this paradigm suffers from inherent limitations, such as lacking explicit probabilities, inadequate coverage, and high computational costs. In this work, we introduce \textbf{Probabilistic Scenarios}, an alternative paradigm designed to address the limitations of sampling. It operates by directly producing a finite set of \{Scenario, Probability\} pairs, thus avoiding Monte Carlo-like approximation. To validate this paradigm, we propose \textbf{TimePrism}, a simple model composed of only three parallel linear layers. Surprisingly, TimePrism achieves 9 out of 10 state-of-the-art results across five benchmark datasets on two metrics. The effectiveness of our paradigm comes from a fundamental reframing of the learning objective. Instead of modeling an entire continuous probability space, the model learns to represent a set of plausible scenarios and corresponding probabilities. Our work demonstrates the potential of the Probabilistic Scenarios paradigm, opening a promising research direction in forecasting beyond sampling.
